No upstream PoC existed (source=no_poc), and the crash's real precondition (MaglevGraphLabeller absent) is unreachable from plain d8 command-line JS in this exact build: v8_flags.maglev_gdbjit is FLAG_READONLY and hard-defaults to true (ENABLE_GDB_JIT_INTERFACE is not compiled into this non-debug build), and the unguarded `|| v8_flags.maglev_gdbjit` clause in MaglevCompiler::Compile (present identically in pre_intro and post_intro -- itself one of the things commit 63226679f9f5 also fixes) therefore always forces a MaglevGraphLabeller to be attached, masking the null-pointer precondition for any end-to-end JS test.

I built ONE standalone C++ harness, /poc/repro_unified.cc, run with the IDENTICAL command on all three versions via run_poc (`exec timeout 30 ./d8` as the final statement so the crash signal/exit code propagates directly). It compiles against each revision's own maglev headers (linked into a custom d8 whose main object is replaced by the harness, so it reuses that build's real compiled Maglev code) and: runs `function f(x){return x+1;} f(1); f;`, builds a real Maglev Graph for the resulting JSFunction via MaglevGraphBuilder::Build() directly (bypassing MaglevCompiler::Compile, so no MaglevGraphLabeller is ever attached -- confirmed via has_graph_labeller()==0 -- exactly the "non-tracing, no --gdbjit" condition named in the fix commit), constructs MaglevReducer<MaglevGraphOptimizer> the same way MaglevGraphOptimizer's own constructor does, then uses SFINAE to call whichever CanInlineCall overload the revision being compiled actually has (that signature is exactly what the intro/fix commits changed), letting each revision's own compiled code decide the outcome.
